sections.heading: C — Learner permit and knowledge test
sections.markdown:
## C — Learner permit and knowledge test

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A06
A Class D license is the non commercial license, and without restrictions it covers any motor vehicle except a commercial motor vehicle. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A06
Truck, bus and other commercial or public service drivers use the Commercial Driver License manual, while motorcycle endorsement seekers use the Motorcycle Operator manual. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A06
Readers should check ct.gov/dmv for the latest laws, the required document list, and the online knowledge test appointment. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A06
Crashes are the top killer of fifteen to nineteen year olds, strike mostly in the first two licensed years, and peak in the first six months. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A06
The brain region that judges risk keeps maturing into the middle twenties, leaving teens short on hazard judgment. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A06
Teen passenger loads raise crash risk, so families must enforce the state passenger limits at home. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A06
Night hours bring deadlier crashes and drowsy driving danger for the young, so the state curfew must be enforced. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A06
Teens wear belts least, yet buckling up is the simplest shield against crash death and grave injury. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A06
Teens face zero tolerance: a single drink already harms driving skill and crash odds. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A06
Calls, passengers, texts, radio tuning, loose pets and like distractions inside the car all lift serious crash risk. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A06
No practice driving starts without a learner permit, and the holder carries it on every drive. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A06
First time license seekers of every age must finish an eight hour Safe Driving Practices class at a Connecticut commercial driving school before licensing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A06
DMV mails a new photo learner permit to each qualified applicant. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A06
Applicants must meet license holder health and fitness standards, and risky medical conditions need a favorable review before any permit issues. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A06
Applicants facing a possible medical review should call the Driver Services Division well ahead at (860) 263-5720. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A07
Permit applicants must be at least sixteen years old. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A07
The permit demands passing a vision test plus a twenty five question knowledge test. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A07
A permit lasts until the driver licenses or for two years from issue, whichever ends first. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A07
Knowledge tests run by appointment with online booking and payment, and the road test books only after the knowledge pass. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A07
The knowledge test spans twenty five questions with twenty correct needed to pass, follows this manual, and offers samples on the DMV mobile app. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A07
Every license class requires vision of at least 20/40 with or without glasses or contacts; an applicant blind in one eye needs 20/40 and a visual field of at least 100 degrees in the other eye. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A07
Driving without required corrective lenses risks a citation at a law enforcement stop. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A07
Eyes deserve a specialist check every year or two, since weak vision hides without testing. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A07
The instructor rides in the front passenger seat, stays alert and ready to take control, and shares responsibility for safe operation with the driver. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]
FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A08
Permit holders of sixteen and seventeen take no passengers except a licensed instructor giving lessons plus companions, or one instructing person at least twenty years old, licensed four or more straight years with no suspension in the prior four. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A08
The passenger ban lifts during live lessons from a licensed instructor of a commercial school or driver education program. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A08
Ignoring permit rules can suspend the permit. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A08
Teen applicants train via a licensed commercial school, a high school program, or home training topped with an eight hour safe driving course holding two parent training hours. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A08
Each teen permit holder’s parent or guardian completes two teaching hours on under eighteen law and teen driving perils inside the required eight hour program. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A08
School courses join thirty classroom hours to forty or more coached road hours, ending in form CS-1, the ticket to the road test. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A08
School graduates test after one hundred twenty permit days; all other applicants wait one hundred eighty days to the driving exam. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A08
Home teaching falls to a qualifier of twenty plus with four suspension free licensed years: a parent, foster parent, guardian, grandparent, married minor’s spouse, or failing those an uncle, aunt, sibling, or stepparent. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A08
At the road test the home teacher signs off the permit, thirty study hours with the eight hour Safe Driving Practices class, full manual coverage, forty coached road hours, and the two hour parent class. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A08
Home trained drivers also file form CS-1a for an approved eight hour course spending four plus hours on alcohol and drug effects, use dangers, abuse penalties, and the mandatory two hour parent class. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A08
Out of state licensed teens of sixteen and seventeen must also take the eight hour course for a Connecticut license. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A08
Thirty classroom hours plus eight commercial coached road hours unlock testing at one hundred twenty days; everyone else waits one hundred eighty days past the permit. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
